public_rationale: On August 12, 2025, Tom’s Guide reported that no tested model beat SimpleBench’s 83.7% human average; GPT-5 ranked fifth behind Gemini 2.5 Pro, Grok 4, and two Claude 4 models [e1]. The test covered over 200 questions involving spatial and temporal reasoning, social intelligence, and tricks [e1]. This supports recurring, substantial failures on commonsense challenge questions within the August 1–12, 2025 assessment window [e1].
limitations: The historical results rely on secondary reporting; the packet contains no dated August 2025 primary leaderboard snapshot.
These challenge results do not establish failure rates across representative everyday user requests. The later benchmark description explicitly identifies trick questions and deliberate traps [e2].
The scores accompanying the August 13, 2026 snapshot do not establish August 2025 performance [e2].
The claim specifies neither a numerical threshold for “often” nor a fixed set of assistants.

statement.excerpt: But she’s right. AI often falls down on basic every day common sense inference.
statement.document_title: LLMs are not like you and me—and never will be.

from_speaker: basic every day common sense inference
our_interpretation: AI means the general-purpose language-model assistants discussed in the post, rather than every form of artificial intelligence.
Often means recurring, substantial failures rather than isolated mistakes; it does not require failure on most questions.
Basic everyday inference includes reasoning about ordinary physical, temporal, and social situations without specialist knowledge.
The ongoing state is assessed during the publication month through August 12, 2025, the latest contemporaneous reporting window.
Benchmarks using ordinary situations can establish recurring weaknesses, but cannot directly estimate the error rate across all everyday user requests.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous evaluations of leading assistants show substantial recurring failures on questions requiring ordinary commonsense inference.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad, relevant contemporaneous evaluations show that such failures are rare across leading assistants and ordinary inference tasks.
